questions.question: It is given the area of a triangle is A. The value of its perimeter, inradius, circumradius and the average of the lengths of the medians are P. r. R and d respectively. The ratio A : P is equal to
questions.solution:
We know that,

A = (r × s)

A = Area of triangle

r = Inradius of triangle

s = semi perimeter of triangle

s = P/2

⇒ A = r × (P/2)

⇒ A : P = r : 2

questions.question: The point at which the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle intersect is known as
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a2578870966179bf6ae60ec039253e4bc3eb3d9dc8aeb846075262dd4cadd7e1.png] 

From the definition “The point of intersection of perpendicular bisector of sides of a triangle is called circum-centre”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ecc19a94681dd82dabf470fb4063d00bec6157575daca8b6d337c62a00df3c4.png] 

The three perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle meet in a single point, called the circumcenter. A point where three or more lines intersect is called a point of concurrency. So, the circumcenter is the point of concurrency of perpendicular bisectors of a triangle.

questions.question: Sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm and 9 cm. What is the radius of the circumcircle of this triangle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The sides of a triangle are 12 cm, 9 cm, and 9 cm

Formula used:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle]

Calculation:

Area of the triangle = √[s (s – a) (s – b) (s – c)] where s = (a + b + c)/2

Side of the triangle are, a = 12 cm, b = 9 cm and c = 9 cm, then

s = (12 + 9 + 9)/2 = 30/2 = 15 cm

Area of the triangle = √[15 (15 – 12) (15 – 9) (15 – 9)] = √[15 × 3 × 6 × 6] = √5 × 6 × 3 = 18√5 cm2

As we know,

Circum-radius of the triangle = abc/[4 × area of triangle] = (12 × 9 × 9)/(4 × 18√5) = (27√5)/10

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: An incircle with center O is drawn inside an equilateral triangle ABC and the length of the side is 12 cm. Find the area (in sq.cm) of the triangle which is not in the incircle.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of equilateral triangle = 12 cm

An incircle with center O is drawn inside an equilateral triangle ABC.

**Concept Used:**

Area of equilateral triangle = √3/4 × side²

Area of circle = πr²

Inradius of equilateral triangle = side/2√3

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217efb580d95020302ae0e7c27b1ed25e532618b70dc9ee2118ca72ce15c3234.png] 

Given that the side length of the equilateral triangle is 12 cm, we can calculate the radius:

⇒ r = (12 / 2√3)

⇒ 6 /(√3)

⇒ 2√3 cm

Now, let's find the area of the incircle using the formula:

Area of incircle = π × r² 

Area of incircle = π × (2√3)²

⇒ 12π cm²

Next, we find the area of the equilateral triangle using the formula:

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × (side)²

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × (12)²

⇒ (√3 / 4) × 144

⇒ 36√3 cm²

Finally, we can subtract the area of the incircle from the area of the equilateral triangle to find the area outside the incircle:

Area outside incircle = Area of equilateral triangle - Area of incircle

⇒ 36√3 cm² - 12π cm²

⇒ 62.32 - 37.68

⇒ 24.64 cm²

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A circle has points P, Q, R on a circle in such a way that angle PQR is 60° and angle QRP is 80°. Calculate the angle subtended by an arc QR at the centre.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔPQR, the sum of all angles is always 180°.

∠QPR = 180° − (60° + 80°) = 40°

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Angle at centre subtended by arc QR = 2 × 40° = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Points P, Q, and R lie on the circle with centre O.

∠PQR = 60° and ∠QRP = 80°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°.

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle.

**Calculations:**

In ΔPQR, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠QRP + ∠QPR = 180°

⇒ 60° + 80° + ∠QPR = 180°

⇒ 140° + ∠QPR = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR = 180° − 140°

⇒ ∠QPR = 40°

Now, arc QR subtends ∠QPR at the circumference and ∠QOR at the centre.

Using the circle property, the central angle is twice the inscribed angle.

⇒ ∠QOR = 2 × ∠QPR

⇒ ∠QOR = 2 × 40°

⇒ ∠QOR = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Subtended by an Arc

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is strictly double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the alternate segment of the circle are always equal to each other.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

If a quadrilateral is inscribed inside a circle, the sum of its opposite angles is always exactly 180°.

questions.question: The in-radius and circumradius of a right-angled triangle is 3 cm and 12.5 cm, respectively. The area of the triangle is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The In-radius and circumradius of a right-angle triangle is 3 cm and 12.5 cm.

**Concept used:**

Inradius of right-angle triangle = (P + B - H)/2

Circumradius of a right angle triangle = H/2

Area of a right angle triangle = (1/2 × P × B)

Where,

P = Perpendicular

B = Base

H = Hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

According to the question

Inradius of right-angle triangle = (P + B – H)/2

⇒ (P + B – H)/2 = 3

⇒ P + B – H = 6 ....(1)

Circumradius of a right angle triangle = H/2

⇒ H/2 = 12.5

⇒ H = 25

Putting the value of H in equation (1)

⇒ P + B – 25 = 6

⇒ P + B = 31

Now,

⇒ (P² + B²) = (25)²

⇒ P² + B² = 625

P + B = 31

⇒ (P + B)² = (31)²

⇒ P² + B² + 2PB = 961

⇒ 2PB = 961 – 625

⇒ PB = 168

So, area of triangle = 1/2 × PB

⇒ (1/2 × 168) = 84 cm² 

**∴ The area of the triangle is 84 cm2 **
